cues.zh: 你有没有回想过脑海深处的记忆，
cues.en: You ever reach way back into your brain

cues.zh: 翻出一些不久前还很常见、显而易见有效，如今却不再流行的东西？
cues.en: and uncover something from the not-too-distant past that seems weirdly obvious yet isn’t popular anymore?

cues.zh: 没错，我说的就是窗户遮阳篷！
cues.en: That’s right, I’m talking about window awnings!

cues.zh: 以前这东西随处可见，尤其是你小时候住家斜对角那些可爱的小砖房上——
cues.en: You used to see these everywhere, especially on those cute brick ranches kitty corner to the house where you grew up -

cues.zh: 我相信大家都有这种共同记忆。
cues.en: I’m sure that’s a universal experience.

cues.zh: 但最近，它们已经不再流行了。
cues.en: But lately, they’ve fallen out of fashion.

cues.zh: 而我想证明，我们应该把它们重新用起来。
cues.en: And I would like to make the case that we should get them back.

cues.zh: 先插句题外话，我不会推荐任何特定类型的遮阳篷或产品系列之类的。
cues.en: Quick programming note, I’m not gonna be recommending any specific kind of awning or product line or anything like that.

cues.zh: 我不是来带货的，
cues.en: I am not here to sell you anything

cues.zh: ……虽然 YouTube 上可能有广告……
cues.en: ...YouTube ads notwithstanding...

cues.zh: 不过我确实很喜欢分享想法。
cues.en: though I do like spreading ideas.

cues.zh: 遮阳篷就是我们祖先想出的妙招之一，但据我所知，我们现在只是觉得自己太酷了，不屑于去用它们。
cues.en: And awnings are one of those ideas that our ancestors figured out but as far as I can tell we just decided we’re too cool for these days.

cues.zh: 这挺讽刺的，因为窗户遮阳篷本来就是用来降温的。
cues.en: Which is ironic because window awnings keep you cool.

cues.zh: 这才是它们的作用！至少是核心作用之一。
cues.en: That’s their point! Or at least, a central point.

cues.zh: 你看，我们都喜欢窗户。
cues.en: See, we like windows.

cues.zh: [Windows XP 报错音] 也许不是这种 Windows，但那种窗户大家基本都喜欢。
cues.en: [WIndows XP error sound] Maybe not that kind, but that kind is pretty universally liked.

cues.zh: 它们能引入自然采光，让我们能看到外面的世界。
cues.en: They let in natural light and allow us to look outside and see things.

cues.zh: 但窗户说到底，也是墙上开的大洞，只是用薄薄几片玻璃堵上了而已。
cues.en: But windows are also great big holes in walls which we only plugged with thin sheets of glass.

cues.zh: 虽然这些年来，它们阻隔热量传递的性能已经好得惊人，
cues.en: While they have gotten surprisingly good over the years at keeping heat energy from moving through them,

cues.zh: 但依然远远比不上周围厚实的墙体。
cues.en: they’re still nowhere near as good as the thick walls which surround them.

cues.zh: 而且，本期视频的关键点来了，
cues.en: And, here’s the important bit to this video,

cues.zh: 当阳光透过窗户照射进来时，它们就会变成主要的吸热源。
cues.en: they become a major source of heat gain when the sun shines through them.

cues.zh: 听说过温室效应吧？
cues.en: Ever heard of the greenhouse effect?

cues.zh: 这不仅发生在温室里，只要太阳能透过透明窗户进入封闭空间，都会出现这种情况。
cues.en: That doesn’t just happen in greenhouses, it happens any time the sun’s energy makes it through a transparent window and into an enclosed space.

cues.zh: 比如你的房子。
cues.en: Like your house.

cues.zh: 阳光一旦照进你家，就会落在室内的各种物体上，比如地板、家具等等。
cues.en: Once sunlight makes its way into your home, it lands on the stuff inside like flooring, furniture, et cetera.

cues.zh: 这些物体吸收了太阳的光能，随后又以热能的形式重新辐射回室内。
cues.en: That stuff absorbs the sun’s light energy which is then re-radiated into your home as heat energy.

cues.zh: 在建筑领域，这种由太阳辐照带来的热量增加被称为日照（insolation）。
cues.en: This heat gain from solar irradiance, in the context of buildings, is called insolation.

cues.zh: 是日照（insolation），不是隔热（insulation）。
cues.en: Not insulation - but insolation.

cues.zh: 别看我，这词又不是我造的。
cues.en: Don’t look at me, I just work here.

cues.zh: 多亏了最近玻璃涂层技术的创新，许多能量都被反射出去，挡在了室外。
cues.en: Thanks to recent innovations in coatings on the glass, a lot of this energy is reflected away and kept out of your home.

cues.zh: 但有趣的是，太阳的威力极其强大，所以哪怕用了极高级的窗户，依然会有大量能量钻进室内，并最终转化为热量。
cues.en: But, fun fact, the sun is extremely powerful so even with really fancy windows there’s a lot of energy getting inside that ultimately becomes heat.

cues.zh: 别光听我说，去问问猫就知道了。
cues.en: Don’t take my word for it, just ask a cat.

cues.zh: 在冬天，这种温暖确实挺舒服的，
cues.en: In the winter months this warmth can be a pretty nice benefit,

cues.zh: 但在夏天——可就遭罪了。
cues.en: but in the summer months - it sucks.

cues.zh: 我们的祖先早就明白这个道理。
cues.en: And our ancestors knew this.

cues.zh: 他们发现，如果建筑物的设计能避开阳光直射窗户，
cues.en: They figured out that if you designed a structure so that the windows couldn’t be in direct sunlight,

cues.zh: 就不会产生温室效应，室内温度也能凉爽得多。
cues.en: then there would be no greenhouse effect and the interior of that structure would stay much cooler.

cues.zh: 你在美国南部很多老式豪宅上见到的那些宽大门廊，可不仅是为了吹风乘凉，
cues.en: Those grand covered porches you see on fancy old houses throughout much of the Southern US weren’t just for enjoying the breeze,

cues.zh: 它们能把窗户完全遮挡在阴凉里。
cues.en: they kept the windows entirely shaded.

cues.zh: 实际上，它们几乎遮住了整栋建筑。
cues.en: In fact they kept pretty much the entire structure shaded.

cues.zh: 而且不仅是庄园大宅——法国区历史建筑上的那些连廊，也同样起到了给建筑降温的作用。
cues.en: And it wasn’t just plantation houses - the galleries attached to historic French Quarter buildings also help keep the buildings cool.

cues.zh: 注意看，这里虽然阳光直射建筑，但除了屋顶，整栋楼几乎都处于阴凉之中。
cues.en: Notice how the building is in direct sunlight here but almost the entire structure (other than the roof) is in shade.

cues.zh: 当然，这些例子其实有一举多得的作用。
cues.en: Of course, those examples have multiple purposes.

cues.zh: 我也不能昧着良心说，给窗户遮阳就是有顶走廊的“唯一目的”。
cues.en: I can’t earnestly say that shading windows was “the point” of a covered porch.

cues.zh: 它还营造了宜人的户外空间，并为门窗遮风挡雨，让你在暴雨天也能开着门窗。
cues.en: It also created a pleasant outdoor space and protected windows and doors from the elements, allowing you to leave them open in a rainstorm.

cues.zh: 但我们确实意识到了这种遮蔽的价值。
cues.en: But we did recognize the value of that coverage.

cues.zh: 正因如此，在不算太遥远的过去，
cues.en: So much so that in the not-too-distant past,

cues.zh: 市面上曾风靡过一些家居产品，它们用最少的材料、最简单的安装，就能提供媲美豪华环绕式走廊的遮阳挡雨效果。
cues.en: there were popular products for your home which provided the shade and cover of an opulent wraparound porch but with minimal materials and easy installation.

cues.zh: 你想问是什么产品？
cues.en: What products, you ask?

cues.zh: 遮阳篷！
cues.en: Awnings!

cues.zh: 这东西似乎在 20 世纪 20 年代曾大行其道。
cues.en: It appears these really came into vogue in the 1920’s.

cues.zh: 这篇刊登在 1927 年《Building Age and National Builder》上的文章一上来就很犀利：
cues.en: This 1927 article in Building Age and National Builder comes out swinging:

cues.zh: “一座没有遮阳棚的漂亮房子，就像一个西装革履却没有打领带的男士。
cues.en: “A Beautiful home which is devoid of awnings resembles a well dressed man without a necktie.

cues.zh: 遮阳棚起到了画龙点睛的作用，恰好为得体的品味画上圆满句号。”
cues.en: The awnings give that finishing touch, just the last point to complete the proper taste.”

cues.zh: 看来作者是真喜欢遮阳棚啊！
cues.en: Seems like the author really likes awnings!

cues.zh: 但这是为什么呢？
cues.en: But why?

cues.zh: 全都是为了住得舒服！
cues.en: It’s all about keeping comfortable!

cues.zh: “门廊上的遮阳棚能让人在午后烈日当头时，依然可以使用门廊。
cues.en: “An awning on the porch permits the use of the porch when the hot afternoon sun is shining.

cues.zh: 它们能让门廊保持阴凉惬意，同时也能降低与门廊相邻房间的室温。”
cues.en: They will keep the porch shady and pleasant, and this also reduces the temperature of the rooms adjoining the porch.”

cues.zh: 而这正是我最喜欢的部分：
cues.en: And here’s my favorite part:

cues.zh: “遮阳棚能挡住直射窗户玻璃的阳光，这在降低室温方面是一大优势，
cues.en: “The fact that the awning excludes the sun from the window glass is quite an important asset in reducing the temperature of the room,

cues.zh: 而且还能防止壁纸和地毯褪色。”
cues.en: and in preventing the fading of wall paper and carpet.”

cues.zh: 看来遮阳棚在当时确实是顶呱呱的好东西！
cues.en: Sure seems like awnings are the cat’s meow!

cues.zh: 1925年，Hal和Helen Davis在《Better Homes and Gardens》杂志上写道
cues.en: In 1925, Hal and Helen Davis wrote in Better Homes and Gardens

cues.zh: “遮阳篷——它有如此多的可能性，如此令人愉悦的可能性，如果买得起却不安装，那这房子真是愚蠢。”
cues.en: “Awnings - they have such possibilities, such delightful possibilities, that foolish indeed is a house to go without them, if they can be afforded.”

cues.zh: 没错，我们刚被Davis一家叫做傻瓜！
cues.en: That’s right, we just got called fools by the Davis family!

cues.zh: 说实话，这篇文章是理解它们如何传播的有用工具。
cues.en: Honestly this article is a useful tool for understanding how they were spreading.

cues.zh: 它甚至按地区细分了遮阳篷配置的差异，以及各种类型的优缺点。
cues.en: It even breaks down the differences in awning configurations by locale and the pros and cons of various types.

cues.zh: 这曾经是件大事！
cues.en: This used to be a big deal!

cues.zh: 它们曾是你房屋的卖点——
cues.en: And they were a selling point for your home -

cues.zh: 房地产公司开始认识到它的价值了！
cues.en: real estate firms are beginning to learn the value!

cues.zh: 而且它们本身就是有趣的装饰点缀。
cues.en: Plus they’re just a fun accent piece.

cues.zh: 我是说，谁不想用一套酷炫的Arabian Awnings来炫耀自己那非同寻常的如画风情呢？
cues.en: I mean, who wouldn’t want to flaunt their unusually picturesque nature with a cool set of Arabian Awnings?

cues.zh: 长矛确实很加分。
cues.en: The spears really sell it.

cues.zh: 但百年前的杂志文章是一回事，现实世界又是另一回事。
cues.en: But hundred year old magazine articles are one thing and the real world is another.

cues.zh: 遮阳篷到底有多大？
cues.en: How big were awnings really?

cues.zh: 嗯，如果你在街景地图上随便逛逛，几乎走访芝加哥任何一个老街区，
cues.en: Well, if you dingle around on the ol’ Streetview and visit practically any old Chicago neighborhood,

cues.zh: 你会发现很多房子至今还装着外窗遮阳篷，伸出来提供遮阴，尤其是朝南和朝西的窗户。
cues.en: you’ll find plenty of houses which still have exterior window awnings providing that overhang for shade, especially on South and West-facing windows.

cues.zh: 从这张图能看出它们多管用：
cues.en: You can see in this image how effective they are:

cues.zh: 房子这一侧正被阳光直射，但遮阳篷几乎完全遮住了下方的窗户。
cues.en: this side of the house is being hit with direct sunlight, but the awning is almost entirely shading the window below it.

cues.zh: 多亏了这个遮阳篷，老式前厅比没有它时凉快得多。
cues.en: Thanks to that awning, the old front room is staying much cooler than it would without it.

cues.zh: 很多这类产品还让你能在下雨时开着窗——至少前提是安装正确，而且窗户类型合适。
cues.en: Many of these products also allowed you to leave windows open in the rain - at least if they were installed correctly and you had the right kind of window.

cues.zh: 他们提供了很多好处！
cues.en: They offered a lot of benefits!

cues.zh: 然而，尽管以各种风格存续至今，
cues.en: Yet despite remaining extant in various styles,

cues.zh: 窗户遮阳篷的功能性用途似乎已几乎完全淡出公众意识。
cues.en: the functional purpose of window awnings seems to have almost entirely left the public consciousness.

cues.zh: 为什么会这样？
cues.en: Why’d this happen?

cues.zh: 我认为这是两个因素的结合：空调和时尚。
cues.en: I’m gonna say it’s a mix of two factors: air conditioning and fashion.

cues.zh: 机械空调的出现削弱了我们过去赖以降温的被动技巧的重要性。
cues.en: The advent of mechanical air conditioning diminished the importance of the passive tricks we used to rely on to keep cool.

cues.zh: 随着越来越多的人开始将耗能的空调接入电网
cues.en: As more and more people started hooking up energy-consuming air conditioners to the power grid

cues.zh: （天哪，希望电网能撑得住……抱歉，跑题了）。
cues.en: (boy I hope it can keep up with all that… sorry wrong topic).

cues.zh: 随着越来越多的人用上空调，家里的温度突然变得可控了。
cues.en: As more and more people got air conditioning, suddenly the temperature in their home was controllable.

cues.zh: 只要那些空调功率足够大，能抵消太阳辐射带来的热量增加，
cues.en: And so long as those air conditioners were powerful enough to overcome the heat gain of solar irradiance,

cues.zh: 那些曾在热浪中帮我们降温的遮阳篷似乎就不再必要了。
cues.en: the awnings that previously helped keep us cool in a heatwave didn’t seem necessary any longer.

cues.zh: 严格来说，它们确实不是。
cues.en: And, technically, they weren’t.

cues.zh: 时间快进一二十年，新建的房子都不装遮阳棚了。
cues.en: So, fast forward a decade or two, and new homes are getting built without them.

cues.zh: 既然能直接把热气抽出去，还要遮阳棚干嘛！
cues.en: No need for awnings when we can pump the heat right out!

cues.zh: 这导致那些装了遮阳棚的老房子，开始显得过时了。
cues.en: That meant that all the older homes with awnings started to look dated.

cues.zh: 而在时尚界，最大的罪过就是“显得过时”。
cues.en: And if there’s one sin in the fashion world, it’s looking dated.

cues.zh: 看得出来，我对待这点是非常认真的。
cues.en: As you can tell I take this very seriously.

cues.zh: 不过抛开时尚不谈，房子上的遮阳棚很可能意味着家里没装空调，
cues.en: Beyond fashion, though, awnings on a home may very well have been a sign that the home didn’t have air conditioning,

cues.zh: 我敢说，20 世纪 60 年代的很多房产中介都建议把它们拆掉。
cues.en: and I’ll bet many a realtor in the 1960’s suggested taking them down.

cues.zh: 他们会说：“没人想要带遮阳棚的房子，那都是老古董和穷人才用的。”
cues.en: "No one wants a house with awnings," they’d say, "those are for old fuddy duddies. And poor people."

cues.zh: 而现在，除了那档电视购物广告，遮阳棚基本上已经被大家遗忘了。
cues.en: And now, other than that one infomercial, awnings are largely forgotten.

cues.zh: 但说真的，我觉得是时候考虑把它们带回来了。
cues.en: But dang it, I think it’s time for us to consider bringing them back.

cues.zh: 首先，我真觉得窗棚挺好看的。
cues.en: For one, I actually think window awnings are pretty cute.

cues.zh: 可能不包括偶尔还能见到的铝制窗棚，不过话说回来——它们确实经久耐用。
cues.en: Maybe not the aluminum ones that you still run across sometimes, though hey - they sure proved their longevity.

cues.zh: 但遮阳棚的款式其实非常丰富，而且还有更多新样式等待发掘。
cues.en: But there are so many different styles of awning out there, plus many more to be discovered.

cues.zh: 就像20年代的人们一样，我认为窗棚确实能为家增添一份个性。
cues.en: And like those 1920’s people, I think window awnings offer a real way to put a personal touch on a home.

cues.zh: 既能展现个性，又能真正帮你遮阳降温，还有比这更酷的吗？
cues.en: And what’s cooler than a way to express yourself that also literally keeps you cool?

cues.zh: 它们的优点实在太多了！
cues.en: There’s a lot to like about them!

cues.zh: 如果有窗棚把骄阳热浪挡在室外，酷暑天气就会好熬得多，
cues.en: Heat waves would be a lot more manageable with window awnings keeping the sun’s heat outside your home,

cues.zh: 而且平时还能帮你省下不少电费。
cues.en: and day to day they save money on electricity bills.

cues.zh: 能省多少钱？
cues.en: How much money?

cues.zh: 额，很遗憾，这个问题并不好回答。
cues.en: Well, unfortunately, that’s not the easiest thing to answer.

cues.zh: 阳光照进窗户时，究竟透进来了多少热能，其实极其难估算。
cues.en: It's annoyingly hard to get an idea of how much heat energy is actually coming through a window when the sun shines through it.

cues.zh: 这取决于太多因素：你所处的地理位置、窗户朝向、一年中的哪个季节、一天中的什么时间，
cues.en: It depends on so many factors: your location on the planet, the direction the window faces, the time of the year, time of day,

cues.zh: 当然，窗户本身的性能也至关重要。
cues.en: and of course the performance of the window itself all matter a lot.

cues.zh: 不过，我还是想给大家提供些有用的参考，所以我联系了一位能使用建筑能耗模拟软件的朋友。
cues.en: Still, I wanted to give you some useful information so I reached out to someone who has access to modeling software which can predict the energy needs of a home.

cues.zh: 他们以芝加哥的一栋典型住宅为例，调整了几个变量，测算了采暖和制冷的能耗需求。
cues.en: They took a typical house in Chicago and ran some numbers for heating and cooling demand while tweaking a few variables.

cues.zh: 这里面有很多有意思的细节，但我最想先强调的是这一点：
cues.en: There’s a lot of interesting stuff to cover here but what I want to highlight first is this:

cues.zh: 房屋不做任何其他改动，仅仅加装窗户遮阳棚，全年的制冷能耗就降低了20%。
cues.en: Doing nothing to the house but adding window overhangs reduced the annual cooling energy needed by 20%.

cues.zh: 这可不是件小事！
cues.en: That’s a big deal!

cues.zh: 但你也会注意到，其他因素也产生了影响。
cues.en: But you’ll notice that other things had an impact, too.

cues.zh: 要是你再仔细看，就会发现这些影响都是一把双刃剑。
cues.en: And if you notice even harder, you’ll see that those impacts were all double-edged.

cues.zh: 过去我曾提到过 Low-E 低辐射玻璃。
cues.en: In the past, I’ve mentioned Low-E windows.

cues.zh: 这算是个统称，本身并没有太具体的含义，但广义上指的就是高性能窗户。
cues.en: That’s kind of a catch-all term and doesn’t mean a whole awful lot on its own, but broadly it just means high-performance windows.

cues.zh: 而窗户的性能指标之一，就是太阳得热系数。
cues.en: And one of a window’s performance metrics is the solar heat gain coefficient.

cues.zh: 你可以把它理解为透过玻璃的太阳热能百分比。
cues.en: You can think of this as the percentage of the sun’s heat energy that makes it through the glass.

cues.zh: 现在市场上有些窗户的 SHGC 极低：有的甚至连四分之一的太阳能都透不过来，
cues.en: There are windows on the market now with exceptionally low SHGCs: some windows don’t even let a quarter of the sun’s energy through,

cues.zh: 这在温暖气候下非常适用，因为你几乎不需要给建筑物供暖。
cues.en: and those are great to have in warm climates where you rarely ever need to heat buildings.

cues.zh: 但对我们北方来说，它们往往不太合适，因为一年里我们需要更多热量而不是制冷，
cues.en: But they’re often not a great fit for us up North because over the course of a year we need more heat energy than we need cooling,

cues.zh: 而挡住太阳免费的热量并不太合理。
cues.en: and blocking the sun’s free heat doesn’t make much sense.

cues.zh: 注意在我们的建模中，
cues.en: Notice that in our modeling,

cues.zh: 仅仅把朝南的窗户换成低SHGC的
cues.en: swapping out just the South facing windows to a lower SHGC

cues.zh: 降低的制冷需求与加装遮阳挑檐的效果相当接近。
cues.en: dropped cooling demand a pretty similar amount to adding overhangs.

cues.zh: 但看看它对供暖需求的影响。
cues.en: But look what it did to the heating demand.

cues.zh: 它显著上升了，因为那些窗户在冬天其实对我们不利。
cues.en: It went up significantly because those windows are actually working against us in the winter.

cues.zh: 我们的冬天很糟糕，来自太阳的免费热量是非常受欢迎的。
cues.en: Our winters suck and some free heat from the sun is a very welcome thing.

cues.zh: 所以改变窗户的热工性能是有取舍的。
cues.en: So there’s a tradeoff to changing the window’s thermal performance characteristics.

cues.zh: 你注意到最低的年总能耗数字来自哪里吗？
cues.en: And have you noticed what the lowest total annual power figure came from?

cues.zh: 既有高太阳得热系数的窗户能在冬天免费取暖，又有挑檐可以在夏天遮挡阳光。
cues.en: Windows with high solar heat gain coefficients for free heating in the winter but which had overhangs to block sunlight in the summer.

cues.zh: 这就是遮阳篷的妙处所在。
cues.en: That’s the beauty of awnings.

cues.zh: 买窗户时，我们不必在冬季和夏季的性能之间做取舍。
cues.en: We don’t have to make the choice between winter and summer performance when buying a window.

cues.zh: 我们可以选最适合冬天吸热的窗户，然后在夏天用遮阳篷挡住阳光就行了。
cues.en: We could use a window best-suited for winter heat gains and then in the summer just block the sun from hitting it with an awning.

cues.zh: 我现在做这个视频的原因是，嗯，我突然意识到
cues.en: The reason why I’m making this video now is that, well, it occurred to me that there isn’t really a difference

cues.zh: 一个安装得当的窗户遮阳篷，和我们今天看到的一些相当先进的住宅设计技术，其实没什么两样。
cues.en: between a properly-installed window awning and some of the rather advanced home design techniques we see today.

cues.zh: 那些在定制新房时预算充足的人，可能会玩点花样，安装各种不同类型的窗户。
cues.en: Those with lots of money to spend when designing their new custom homes might get fancy and install different window types.

cues.zh: 我之前讲过一种方法，就是在屋檐下方安装高得热窗户，这样冬天能免费供暖，夏天又不会。
cues.en: One method I’ve talked about before is installing high heat-gain windows below an overhang so they provide that free heat in the winter but not in the summer.

cues.zh: 然后在房子的其他地方用低得热窗户。
cues.en: And then use low-heat-gain windows elsewhere in the house.

cues.zh: 这想法挺酷，但跟直接装个遮阳篷比起来，工作量太大了！
cues.en: That’s a cool idea but it’s a lot of work compared to slapping on an awning!

cues.zh: 而装遮阳篷最棒的一点（除了说起来很好玩之外）是它便宜，而且哪儿都能装！
cues.en: And the best thing about slapping on an awning (besides how fun that is to say) is that it can be done cheaply and anywhere!

cues.zh: 说到哪儿都能装，这里有一段笨拙的配音剪辑。
cues.en: Speaking of anywhere, here’s a clunky voiceover edit.

cues.zh: 我担心自己太专注于我们这里面临的情况，而对温暖和炎热气候关注不够。
cues.en: I’m worried that I fixated too much on the scenario we face here and not enough on warm and hot climates.

cues.zh: 因为即使你装了市面上最棒的窗户，SHGC只有0.2，五扇中等大小的朝西窗户（我按3乘5英尺算中等）
cues.en: Because even if you’ve got the best dang windows on the market with an SHGC of .2, five average-sized West-facing windows (I’m calling 3 by 5 feet average)

cues.zh: 每天下午也会有好几个小时让超过一千瓦的热量进来。
cues.en: are going to let in more than a kilowatt of heat for several hours every afternoon.

cues.zh: 这和把空间加热器开到高档运行差不多，而外面气温高达100华氏度时，这可不是什么明智之举。
cues.en: That’s not far off from running a space heater on high, and when it’s 100 degrees outside that’s not the smartest move.

cues.zh: 出于好奇，我决定去看看亚利桑那州凤凰城附近正在新建的一些住宅
cues.en: For giggles I decided to look at some new homes getting built around Phoenix, Arizona

cues.zh: 坦白说，我很惊讶在那个气候条件下，显然没人关注窗户的遮阳挑檐。
cues.en: and it’s frankly astonishing to me that in that climate there’s apparently no focus paid on window overhangs.

cues.zh: 当然，过去我们没有现在这种高级玻璃，
cues.en: Sure, back in the day we didn’t have the fancy glass we do now,

cues.zh: 但如果遮阳篷在芝加哥这里很流行——而这里一年真正热的也就4……也许5个月——
cues.en: but if window awnings were popular here in Chicago, where it’s really only hot 4… maybe 5 months of the year,

cues.zh: 在我看来，不想办法给窗户遮阴，浪费了大量的能源和金钱。
cues.en: it seems to me like there’s a lot of energy and money being wasted by not thinking of ways to keep windows in the shade.

cues.zh: 现在，我想补充几点说明。
cues.en: Now, there's a couple of notes I want to add.

cues.zh: 我自己和协助我做建模的人都对它输出的一些数据有点怀疑。
cues.en: Both myself and the person who helped me with the modeling here are a bit skeptical of some of the data it spat out.

cues.zh: 在已经有 2.5 英尺屋檐的情况下，拉上深色窗帘的影响看起来实在太高了，
cues.en: The impact of dark closed drapes when there’s already a 2.5 foot overhang seems really high,

cues.zh: 而且光靠这些窗帘降低的制冷功耗，居然比屋檐还多，这似乎……不太可能。
cues.en: and the fact that those drapes by themselves are lowering cooling power more than the overhangs seems… impossible.

cues.zh: 挂在窗户内侧的窗帘，根本无法阻止阳光穿透窗玻璃。
cues.en: Drapes on the inside of a window don’t stop sunlight from passing through the window glass.

cues.zh: 充其量，如果反光性特别好，它们能把一部分太阳辐射能量反射回去，
cues.en: At best, if they’re very reflective, they can push some of the sun's energy back out

cues.zh: 但我以前站在朝西的窗户边，即使拉着白色卷帘，也能亲身感受到夏天的午后那卷帘烫得要命。
cues.en: but having stood next to a West-facing window with a white roller shade, I can say from experience that that shade gets pretty stinking hot on summer afternoons.

cues.zh: 最好的办法始终是起初就别让阳光穿透玻璃，这样就不会产生温室效应，
cues.en: It is always better to keep the sun from coming through the glass in the first place, that way there is no greenhouse effect,

cues.zh: 所以这个模型对这些因素的考量方式，看起来有点问题。
cues.en: so how this model is considering those factors seems a bit off.

cues.zh: 说真的，如果非要我在这里呼吁点什么，那就是我们需要更多针对窗户遮阳篷效果的研究。
cues.en: Really, if there’s one call to action I want to make here it would be that there needs to be more study on the effectiveness of window awnings.

cues.zh: 关于这个话题的信息少得离谱，
cues.en: It’s quite strange how little information there is on this topic,

cues.zh: 而且我能找到的大多是遮阳篷厂家的宣传，我并不能全信。
cues.en: and most of what I’ve found are claims from awning manufacturers so I’m not exactly taking them seriously.

cues.zh: 但在我看来这显而易见：只要你能阻隔透过窗户的阳光直射，
cues.en: But it does seem pretty obvious to me that if you can eliminate direct sunlight transmission through a window,

cues.zh: 那就相当于把任何一扇窗都变成了朝北的窗户，不管它原本朝向哪里。
cues.en: then you’re effectively turning any window into a North-facing window no matter which side of your house it’s on.

cues.zh: 而这在一年的炎热季节里，效果可能会天差地别。
cues.en: And that could make a dramatic difference in the warm parts of the year.

cues.zh: 当然除非你在南半球，那样的话，当我没说——反过来才对。
cues.en: Unless you’re in the Southern hemisphere in which case, strike that - reverse it.

cues.zh: 不过，遮阳篷也并非完全没有缺点。
cues.en: Now, it’s not like awnings don’t come with any drawbacks.

cues.zh: 最显而易见的一点，就是它们会让室内在白天变得暗得多。
cues.en: Most obvious is that they make the interior of your home much darker during the day.

cues.zh: 如果遮阳篷是用半透明材料做的，窗户依然能透进不少柔和的漫射光，
cues.en: If the awning is made of a translucent material you could still get plenty of filtered light coming through the window,

cues.zh: 但它存在的全部目的就是挡掉直射阳光，如果你或你的猫很喜欢晒太阳，那装了遮阳篷可就完全晒不到了。
cues.en: but its entire purpose is to eliminate direct sunlight and if that’s something you or your cat appreciates, well a proper awning is going to eliminate it.

cues.zh: 不过，我倒是很好奇，用超低太阳能得热系数的玻璃做成透明遮阳篷，效果到底会怎么样。
cues.en: Although, I am quite curious about the potential effectiveness of a transparent awning made from glass with a really low solar heat gain coefficient.

cues.zh: 这或许是个两全其美的好办法。
cues.en: That might be a way to have the best of both worlds.

cues.zh: 而且几乎不会遮挡你看向天空的视线。
cues.en: And it would leave your view of the sky mostly unimpeded.

cues.zh: 再来就是维护问题了。
cues.en: Then there’s maintenance.

cues.zh: 现在还能见到的那些铝制遮阳篷，最初就是为了解决高档织物打理起来太麻烦而设计的。
cues.en: The aluminum ones that still hang around were designed in response to the fiddle factor of fancy fabrics.

cues.zh: 这些织物会随时间褪色，还需要定期清洁，而且根据支撑结构的设计，
cues.en: Those fabrics would fade with time and required periodic cleaning, and depending on the design of the support structure,

cues.zh: 从遮阳篷上拆下织物可能非常麻烦。
cues.en: removing the fabric from the awning could be a pain in the butt.

cues.zh: 由铝制成的刚性遮阳篷基本解决了这些问题，这很可能就是它们开始普及的原因。
cues.en: A rigid awning made of aluminum mostly took care of these problems, and that’s most likely why they started spreading.

cues.zh: 不过话说回来，自从遮阳篷不再流行以来，材料科学已经有了巨大的进步，
cues.en: Then again, materials science has improved dramatically since awnings went out of fashion,

cues.zh: 而且有些织物遮阳篷可以按需展开。
cues.en: and some fabric awnings can be selectively deployed.

cues.zh: 卷帘式遮阳篷可以在你不需要或不想要的时候收起来，
cues.en: A roller-awning can be retracted when you don’t need or want it,

cues.zh: 而且别不信，只要加入Wi-Fi和执行器，
cues.en: and don’t look now but throw some Wi-Fi and actuators into the mix

cues.zh: 你就能拥有一个智能遮阳篷，它可以按需精确展开，并在阴天或恶劣天气时保持收起。
cues.en: and you’ve got yourself a Smart Awning that could deploy exactly as much as needed and stay retracted on cloudy days or in inclement weather.

cues.zh: 我想到的遮阳棚最后一个主要缺点，就是虫害。
cues.en: The last main drawback to awnings that I can think of is pests.

cues.zh: 在为窗户遮风挡雨的同时，你也给各种生物提供了庇护所，虽然窗外有个知更鸟窝我倒挺乐意，
cues.en: Through providing shelter for your window you’re also providing shelter for living creatures, and while I’d be pretty cool with a robin’s nest outside my window,

cues.zh: 但要是来个马蜂窝就没那么美妙了。
cues.en: a wasp nest is less cool.

cues.zh: 不过话说回来，如果窗户装了纱窗，其实影响也没那么大，
cues.en: Then again, if the window is screened it’s not like that really matters all that much

cues.zh: 但我以前处理过不少马蜂窝，能不碰上自然是最好的。
cues.en: but I’ve dealt with my share of wasp nests and usually it’s best to not have to deal with them.

cues.zh: 不过说实话，在我看来这些缺点都微不足道，而且很多时候根本算不上问题。
cues.en: But to be honest, all of those drawbacks seem pretty minor to me, and many of them aren’t even a thing all the time.

cues.zh: 我真的特别想给家里装几个遮阳棚——尤其是西边那侧。
cues.en: I can tell you that I would freaking love some awnings on my home - particularly on the West side.

cues.zh: 我目前依然坚持只在后半夜开空调，
cues.en: I’m still doing that thing where I only run the air conditioning in the overnight hours

cues.zh: 而这种做法带来的一个特别有趣的发现，就是日照的影响极其显著。
cues.en: and one of the most interesting things that technique has revealed is the dramatic effect of the sun.

cues.zh: 阴天的时候，就算外面挺热，我家里一整天下来也才升温五六华氏度。
cues.en: On cloudy days, even though it might be quite hot outside, my home only heats up by 5 or 6 degrees Fahrenheit over the course of the day.

cues.zh: 但如果是同样温度的晴天，升温幅度几乎就翻倍了。
cues.en: But if it’s a sunny day at the same temperature, that just about doubles.

cues.zh: 当然，这不全是因为窗户进来的热量——阁楼被太阳晒得滚烫，墙壁也是。
cues.en: Of course, not all of that is heat from the windows - the attic’s also getting stupid hot from the sun, and so are the walls.

cues.zh: 所以很难把这一个变量单独剥离出来。
cues.en: So it’s not easy to isolate that variable.

cues.zh: 但我敢说，一旦阳光直射西边的窗户，那些房间升温的速度真的非常惊人。
cues.en: But I can say it is truly remarkable how quickly the rooms on the West side start to heat up once the sun reaches those windows.

cues.zh: 当然，遮阳篷并不是唯一的解决办法。
cues.en: Awnings aren’t the only solution, of course.

cues.zh: 很多欧洲网友早就按捺不住想在评论区科普了，说他们那边早就用上了室外卷帘。
cues.en: There’s been a whole bunch of Europeans just champing at the commenting bit to let you know all about those exterior roller shutters they’ve had over there for a while.

cues.zh: 这些挺有意思的，本地也开始卖了，
cues.en: Those are interesting, and they’re starting to be sold here,

cues.zh: 但我很好奇，这些卷帘在太阳底下会变得多烫。
cues.en: but I’m curious to know how hot those shutters get in the sun.

cues.zh: 关上时，它们和窗户玻璃之间似乎会困住一些空气，所以虽然遮阳效果毋庸置疑，
cues.en: When closed they seem to trap a bit of air between them and the window glass, so while I have no doubt they’re blocking the sun,

cues.zh: 但在我看来，卷帘把吸收的热量辐射到那层空气里，窗户肯定会变得相当热。
cues.en: it seems to me like the window will be getting quite warm as the shutters radiate their absorbed heat into that airspace.

cues.zh: 我更愿意装遮阳棚，这样热量就不会被困住，而且我还能看外面的风景！
cues.en: I’d rather have an awning, then that heat isn’t trapped and I can still look outside!

cues.zh: 然后就是室外百叶帘。我发现这东西越来越多了，通常装在门廊上。
cues.en: Then there are exterior blinds. I’m starting to see these spread, often on porches.

cues.zh: 它们和 Rolladen 原理基本一样，但通常是布料做的，也没有集成到窗框之类的结构里。
cues.en: They’re basically the same idea as Rolladen but usually fabric and not integrated into the window frame or anything.

cues.zh: 同样，挡住阳光直射窗户绝对没问题，但用的时候也会挡住视线，而遮阳棚就不会，
cues.en: Again, those will absolutely do the job of blocking sunlight from hitting the window, but they also block the view when in use which awnings don’t,

cues.zh: 至少不会挡住往外看的视线。
cues.en: at least not the view out.

cues.zh: 要是我看起来对遮阳篷特别狂热，没错，我就是！
cues.en: If I seem gung-ho about awnings, well I am!

cues.zh: 我觉得它们很酷，而且在过去的半个世纪里被严重忽视了。
cues.en: I think they’re cool and have been tragically overlooked for the past half-century.

cues.zh: 这就让我想到最后一件事。
cues.en: Which brings me to one last thing.

cues.zh: 我住联排别墅，这意味着如果我想装窗户遮阳篷，就得惊动业委会。
cues.en: I live in a townhome which means if I wanted to install window awnings, I’d need to get the HOA involved.

cues.zh: 那可一点都不好玩。
cues.en: And that’s not fun.

cues.zh: 所以——回到我之前呼吁大家对它们做更多研究的话题，
cues.en: So - circling back to that earlier call to action where I said we should do more research on them,

cues.zh: 如果事实证明窗户遮阳篷真能让普通家庭的制冷成本降低 20%，
cues.en: if it turns out that window awnings actually could reduce a typical home’s cooling costs by 20%,

cues.zh: 那要不我们干脆剥夺业委会禁止安装遮阳篷的权力怎么样？
cues.en: then whaddya say we go ahead and neuter an HOA’s ability to forbid their installation?

cues.zh: 或者，如果觉得这太激进了，至少强制业委会提供一批获批的款式和颜色供选择。
cues.en: Or, if that sounds too extreme, at the very least force HOAs to offer an assortment of approved styles and colors.

cues.zh: 直觉告诉我，随着这种“热穹顶”现象不断出现，我们会想方设法寻找更多不同的降温方式，
cues.en: Something tells me we’re going to want to find more and different ways to keep cool as these heat domes keep happening,

cues.zh: 要是像窗户遮阳篷这么简单的东西真有看上去那么有用，额，我们大概应该鼓励大家去用。
cues.en: and if something as simple as a window awning is as useful as it seems to be, uhh we should probably encourage their use.

cues.zh: 好啦，就先聊到这儿！
cues.en: Alright, well that’s it!

cues.zh: 如果各位里有人从事建筑节能规范评估或相关好玩的工作，欢迎随时分享你手头的信息。
cues.en: If anyone out there is involved in evaluating building energy codes and all that fun stuff, please chime in with any info you might have on this topic.

cues.zh: 我确实没查到专门针对遮阳篷能节省多少制冷费用的资料，
cues.en: I really didn’t find anything specifically about awnings and how much they could reduce cooling costs,

cues.zh: 而且据我所知，除了极少数硬核圈子，大家基本都不怎么关注窗户挑檐的效果。
cues.en: and from what I’ve heard there really isn’t much attention paid to the effects of window overhangs at all outside of hyper-nerd circles.

cues.zh: 如果遮阳篷在空调出现前就管用，那放到现在肯定也依然管用。
cues.en: If window awnings were helpful before air conditioning, then surely they’re still helpful now.

cues.zh: 而眼看着现在很多新房——哪怕是在亚利桑那这种地方——盖的时候都完全不装窗户挑檐，
cues.en: And given how a lot of new housing stock, even in places like Arizona, is getting built without window overhangs at all,

cues.zh: 要么是这些新型窗户神到不行，要么就是我们单纯把老祖宗的妙招给忘光了。
cues.en: either these new windows are miraculous marvels or we just kinda forgot the tricks of the past.

cues.zh: 来，给其中一些再试一次。
cues.en: Here’s to giving some of them another go.

cues.zh: ♫ 丝滑得不得了的爵士乐 ♫
cues.en: ♫ blisteringly smooth jazz ♫

cues.zh: ……基本上大家都喜欢。
cues.en: …pretty universally liked.

cues.zh: 它们让自然光进来，让我们能看到外面的东西！
cues.en: They let in natural light and allow us to look outside and see things!

cues.zh: 但是……那是什么？
cues.en: But… what was that?

cues.en: Probably nothing you heard but I stopped anyway.

cues.en: Those grand covered porches you see on fancy…

cues.en: They will keep the porch shaft and pleasant,

cues.en: and this also reduces the temperature - I can skip the rest of this line because I already recorded the thing with the tie.
